evidence: create-product-dto.ts: CreateProductDto uses only @IsString/@IsNumber structural checks; its comment says domain invariants live in the value-object validators, so nothing is duplicated
create-product.command.ts: CreateProductCommand constructor(product: CreateProductDto) copies name/description/price as readonly fields
create-product.service.ts: CreateProductService.execute builds new CreateProductCommand(dto) and sends it via commandBus.execute<CreateProductCommand, string>

create-product.command-handler.ts: @CommandHandler(CreateProductCommand) execute() calls Product.create(Name.create, Description.create, Price.create), checks product.isValid / brokenRules, then saves and commits events
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All four files cover one concern, the create-product use case, and each file has a distinct role. CreateProductDto is the transport contract. It checks only structure, and its doc comment says domain invariants (Name 3–100 chars, positive Price) stay out of it on purpose, so no rule is duplicated. CreateProductCommand carries the DTO's fields onto the command bus. CreateProductService builds the command and dispatches it through CommandBus. CreateProductCommandHandler is the single place that assembles the aggregate. It builds the domain value objects (Name.create, Description.create, Price.create) and calls Product.create, then turns broken rules into a BrokenRulesException, persists the product and commits its events. No file skips the module's own flow (service → command → handler), and no invariant shows up in two places. The handler takes the concrete ProductRepository from infrastructure, but that is a layer-dependency question, which is out of scope here.
